findings.title: Backup code plus any non-empty totpCode bypasses the password check
findings.body: `authorize` only verifies the password when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (line 121). The new branch at line 131 runs whenever `backupCode` is present and never looks at `totpCode`. So an attacker can POST `email`, a valid `backupCode` and an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` such as "x": the password check is skipped and the bogus TOTP is never validated. The result is a login with only the email address and one backup code. Fix this by always requiring a valid password for CAL-identity users when a backup code is used (or by rejecting requests that send both fields), instead of tying the password check to the absence of `totpCode`.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The encrypted code list is read with the user (line 73), checked in memory, then written back with the used entry set to null. Nothing guards against concurrent requests. Two simultaneous logins with the same code both read the old list, both pass, and both write. A single-use backup code can therefore be redeemed more than once. One request can also overwrite another's consumption of a different code, resurrecting it. Use a transaction or an optimistic check, e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and treat a zero row count as failure.

findings.title: MissingBackupCodes is not reported once codes run out, and the message points to a feature that doesn't exist
findings.body: Used codes are replaced with `null`, so after all ten are consumed `user.backupCodes` is still a non-empty ciphertext. The user then gets `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than `MissingBackupCodes`. Separately, the `missing_backup_codes` text says "Please generate them in your settings", but there is no regeneration UI. Users who enabled 2FA before this feature, or who used every code, can only get new codes by disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

findings.title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable and resetState
findings.body: Once `/totp/enable` succeeds, 2FA is active on the server and the modal switches to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the explicit Close button calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()`. Dismissing the dialog with Escape or a click outside goes through `onOpenChange` and calls neither. The parent then still shows 2FA as disabled. Reopening the modal lands back on the backup-codes step with stale codes. The blob URL is also never revoked.

findings.title: Backup code matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive
findings.body: Codes are lowercase hex, and the input is compared after stripping only dashes. A user who types the code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace or a trailing newline from the downloaded file, gets `IncorrectBackupCode`. Normalize the input with `trim()` and `toLowerCase()` here and in `disable.ts`.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in the body causes an unhandled 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called on unvalidated JSON input. A truthy non-string value such as a number or an object throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400. Validate the body, for example with zod, before using it.

findings.title: No tests exercise backup-code login or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: None of the new authentication paths are tested: login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The first test also no longer closes the new backup-codes screen, and its switch assertion is acknowledged (FIXME) to pass even when the switch is not checked. These gaps let security regressions in the new code go undetected.
